name: Pink Coral
lede: Pink Coral is a warm, soft pink named for the sea animal's skeleton; as a color name it is a twentieth-century dictionary entry, and the books mention it only in passing.

sections.title: A name from the sea
sections.body: The name pairs [[pink]] with [[coral]], the material that gives the color its picture [2]. Maerz and Paul's dictionary of 1930 records it as first used in 1926, and it enters the ISCC-NBS system as a form of deep pink [2]. Nothing in our sources says who coined it [2].

sections.title: Pink coral in the books
sections.body: The only book mention in our collection is incidental. In her fabric book, Finlay describes a woman making bark cloth who wears a shell headband hung with small sections of pink coral that sway as she moves [1]. It is a scene about tapa, not about a color name, and it shows pink coral as a worked material for adornment [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive it appears in 0.05% of paintings (13), rarer than 79% of the named colors, as photographed [3]. The earliest match is a painting of 1650, some 280 years before the name's 1926 record, so it is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph [3].

disambiguation.gloss: a stronger orange-pink, the standard CSS coral
